item.title: Dolphins, Colts will stage a "someone has to win" game
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Colts need a lot more than a horseshoe to turn their season around.
item.content:encoded:
The Colts need a lot more than a horseshoe to turn their season around. But they got some good luck from the scheduling gods on Sunday, in the form of a visit from the Dolphins.

Both teams are struggling to say the least. Via NBC Sports research, the 1-7 Dolphins rank 31st in scoring offense, with 15.8 points per game. They're also 28th in total offense, at 282.3 yards per game.

The Dolphins have been held to 13 or fewer points in five games this season. That's the most in the league.

And they're starting Kyle McCord at quarterback, because Malik Willis is on injured reserve.

The Colts haven't been much better. They've lost five in a row since starting the season 2-2. Since Week 12 of the 2025 season, they're 2-14. That's the worst record over that span in the entire league.

So, yes, someone has to win. Unless there's a tie. Which would complicate the four-official road trip to Cincinnati.

item.title: Report: Baker Mayfield uncertain for Week 11 due to lower-leg injury
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Buccaneers are on their bye week and they're hoping that quarterback Baker Mayfield will be able to play when they return to action in Week 11.
item.content:encoded:
The Buccaneers are on their bye week and they're hoping that quarterback Baker Mayfield will be able to play when they return to action in Week 11.

Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports that Mayfield has been dealing with a lower-leg injury that he suffered in the team's Week 9 loss to the Bears. Mayfield did not leave the 27-24 loss, but Garafolo reports that he has been in a walking boot at times this week.

While Mayfield's availability for next weekend's game in Detroit is in question, he is not expected to miss extended time as a result of the injury. That's good news for the Buccaneers as their 3-6 record leaves them without too much room to drop more games while remaining in the race for the NFC South title.

Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels started three games while Mayfield was out with a dislocated thumb and he would be in line to start again if Mayfield is unable to go.

item.title: Four officials in all will make the road trip from Indy to Cincinnati
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: It's officially a road trip.
item.content:encoded:
It's officially a road trip.

The chaos caused by Friday's nationwide ground stop prompted the NFL to get very creative with its officiating assignments. That creativity includes four officials getting in a car and traveling from Indianapolis to Cincinnati to work a doubleheader separated by 110 miles.

Via Aditi Kinkhabwala of CBS, backup referee Don Willard will be joined by umpire Terry Killens (pictured), field judge Jabir Walker, and side judge Justin Larrew in the effort to officiate two games in one day: Dolphins-Colts and Steelers-Bengals.

Per the league, not at least since 1970 has an official worked two games in one day.

The full scope of the changes to the usual crew won't be publicly known until the games are completed and the official Game Books are posted by the league; each one includes the full list of officials by position.

It there are glitches, some will ask why the NFL resorted to such an extreme plan to ensure that there will be enough officials at every game. They use crews for a reason. On Sunday, those crews apparently will be obliterated.

item.title: Jahmyr Gibbs totals 171 yards in first half as Lions roll over Patriots
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: For the second consecutive week, the Patriots' defense is having a rough game.
item.content:encoded:
Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs is making a mockery of the Patriots' defense today in Munich, Germany.

Gibbs has 171 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown as the Lions have cruised to a 21-3 lead late in the second quarter. Gibbs has 13 carries for 93 yards and a touchdown, plus another four catches for 78 receiving yards. The Patriots' defense has had no answer for him.

It's the second consecutive ugly outing for New England's defense, which was shredded by the Packers' passing game last week.

The Patriots' offense is also struggling, but that appears to be mostly due to the injury suffered by quarterback Drake Maye on New England's opening possession. The Patriots had been marching down the field until Maye was sacked by Aidan Hutchinson on third-and-goal, and Maye was knocked out of the game with an ankle injury. After the field goal immediately following that sack, the Patriots haven't scored.

It's hard to imagine the Patriots mounting a second-half comeback with Tommy DeVito at the helm, but that's what they'll have to do if they're going to avoid heading home from Germany on a two-game losing streak.

item.title: Drake Maye out for game with ankle injury after getting sacked by Aidan Hutchinson
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Hutchinson was also injured after he got up and celebrated.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots quarterback Drake Maye will miss the rest of today's game in Germany.

Maye has been ruled out with an ankle injury after he was sacked by Aidan Hutchinson on the final play of the Patriots' first offensive drive.

Hutchinson tackled Maye from behind and landed on the back of Maye's legs. It was similar to the type of injury that can be caused by a hip-drop tackle or a horse-collar tackle, but it wasn't a penalty, just an unfortunate play for Maye.

Patriots backup quarterback Tommy DeVito is in for Maye. Seventh-round rookie Behren Morton is the only other quarterback on the Patriots' roster.

Hutchinson was also injured after the sack when he got up, jumped high into the air in celebration and then landed awkwardly. The Lions say he's questionable to return with a knee injury.

The Lions lead 14-3 late in the second quarter.

item.title: Drake Maye limps to locker room, Tommy DeVito in at QB for Patriots in Germany
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Maye was injured when Aidan Hutchinson sacked him. Hutchinson was also injured while celebrating the sack.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots quarterback Drake Maye suffered an injury on the last play of New England's first offensive possession today in Germany.

On a third-and-goal, Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson took Maye down and appeared to land on his legs. Maye was slow to get up but walked off the field on his own, and there was initially no indication that he was seriously injured.

But at the start of the Patriots' second drive, Maye limped to the locker room and backup Tommy DeVito came in to replace him. The Patriots said Maye is questionable to return with an ankle injury.

Hutchinson was also injured while celebrating his sack of Maye, and he's currently in the locker room as well. The Lions said Hutchinson is questionable to return with a knee injury.

Patriots right tackle Morgan Moses has also left the game with an injury.

The Lions have an early 7-3 lead, but the injuries to two of the best players in the NFL may prove to matter more to both teams' playoff hopes than the result of this game.

item.title: German fan favorite Amon-Ra St. Brown scores first TD in Munich
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Amon-Ra St. Brown, whose mother is German and who spent some of his childhood in Germany, scored the game's first touchdown today.
item.content:encoded:
Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown has a German mother, speaks German and spent some of his childhood in Germany, so when the NFL sent the Lions to Munich, they knew he'd be a fan favorite. And it didn't take St. Brown long to deliver.

On the Lions' first possession, St. Brown caught a pass from Jared Goff, made the first tackler miss, cut back inside and raced to the end zone for a 56-yard touchdown.

The Lions completed two passes on the opening drive and St. Brown caught them both, for 63 yards.

Detroit has an early 7-3 lead over the Patriots.

item.title: Aidan Hutchinson injured celebrating after sacking Drake Maye in Germany
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Lions' best defensive player went down after a third-and-goal sack.
item.content:encoded:
Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson was injured celebrating after sacking Drake Maye on third-and-goal at the end of the Patriots' first possession early Sunday in Munich, Germany.

Maye appeared to be banged up on the sack as well, but Hutchinson got up, jumped in the air celebrating, and then immediately seemed to feel something wrong as he landed. He fell to the ground and grabbed at his right lower leg.

Hutchinson was able to walk off the field with a limp. After getting examined on the sideline for a few minutes, he walked to the locker room with the Lions' medical staff. There was no immediate word on the nature of his injury.

The Patriots kicked a field goal to take a 3-0 lead.

item.title: A.J. Brown, Amon-Ra St. Brown active for Patriots-Lions in Munich
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Brown returns to the Patriots lineup after missing the last two games.
item.content:encoded:
The Patriots and Lions each listed their top wide receiver as questionable to play in Sunday's game in Munich and both teams will have their leading wideouts in the lineup.

A.J. Brown is active for New England after missing the last two games with a knee injury. Brown also missed four games with an ankle injury earlier in the season, so this will be just his fourth appearance of the year.

Amon-Ra St. Brown has been dealing with a rib injury, but it would have taken a lot for him to miss this game. St. Brown's mother is German, he speaks the language and he's talked often about how much Sunday's game means to him.

Running back Rhamondre Stevenson is also active for the Patriots. Stevenson has a knee injury that led to him being listed as questionable and his presence is important as the Patriots remain without TreVeyon Henderson.

Safety Brenden Schooler, guard Walter Rouse, offensive tackle Dametrious Crownover, quarterback Behren Morton, guard Ben Brown, and cornerback Carlton Davis are inactive for the Patriots. Cornerback D.J. Reed, center Cade Mays, defensive back Keith Abney, linebacker Amen Ogbongbemiga, defensive lineman Mekhi Wingo, and defensive end Ahmed Hassanein are out for Detroit.

item.title: Demarvion Overshown wasn't fined for running onto field in street clothes
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In the fourth quarter of a Week 9 game the Cowboys led by only three points, Dallas forced — and recovered — a fumble by Colts running back Jonathan Taylor.
item.content:encoded:
In the fourth quarter of a Week 9 game the Cowboys led by only three points, Dallas forced — and recovered — a fumble by Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. The ensuing celebration drew a penalty.

Said referee Clay Martin in announcing the specific of theinfraction, "Unsportsmanlike conduct by Dallas, who had a non-uniformed player in the blue sweats and a stocking cap come onto the field to celebrate."

The non-uniformed player in the blue sweats and the stocking cap was linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who was inactive for the game due to injury.

While violations of the celebration rules routinely spark fines, Overshown was not financially penalized by the league.

It's possible Overshown got some sort of punishment from the team, especially since owner and G.M. Jerry Jones rejected Overshown's claim that he didn’t know it was against the rules for a player not in uniform to run onto the field for a celebration.

"I don’t think that," Jones said. "I really don't. I think that he's been involved in football at Texas, and he's been involved here, and he knows that, at every level, a nonparticipant can't run out on the field."

Every player should have known the rule before last Sunday. Given what happened in the Dallas game, where the lost 15 yards of field position set the stage for a game-tying field goal by the Colts (the Cowboys eventually won, 27-23), there's even less of an excuse to not know it now.

item.title: Bill Belichick on Louisville-UNC brawl: "That's not what we're here for"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Saturday's game between Louisville and North Carolina ended in a brawl, sparked apparently by the Tar Heels being a little too aggressive in defending a victory-formation play.
item.content:encoded:
Saturday's game between Louisville and North Carolina ended in a brawl, sparked apparently by the Tar Heels being a little too aggressive in defending a victory-formation play. After UNC's 16-14 loss to the Cardinals, Carolina coach Bill Belichick addressed the brouhaha.

"You play the game between the whistles, that’s not what we’re here for," Belichick said, via the Associated Press. "We got out there and got everybody out as quickly as possible."

Footage from WRAL shows Belichick involved in the effort to clean up the mess, pulling several of his players away from the fray.

It started when North Carolina defensive tackle Xavier Lewis and Louisville offensive lineman Johnnie Brown III got engaged in some pushing and shoving. The situation spread into various confrontations as the benches emptied.

The next question is whether discipline will be issued, by the individual teams or the ACC. No penalties were enforced, because the game ended in the early stages of the altercation.

At 5-5, the Tar Heels need a full roster next weekend, if they hope to become bowl-eligible with a win over Virginia. The season ends with a game against NC State.

item.title: Starting with Patriots-Lions, Fox has three windows on Sunday
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The last of the early-morning 2026 kickoffs happens today, with the Patriots playing the Lions in Germany.
item.content:encoded:
The last of the early-morning 2026 kickoffs happens today, with the Patriots playing the Lions in Germany. Unlike the others, which were televised by NFL Network, the Week 10 European game will be carried by Fox.

That gives Fox three windows in one day, with the morning game followed by the usual 1:00 p.m. ET window and the every-other-week 4:25 p.m. ET window.

Most of the country will see Vikings-Packers, featuring the return of Kirk Cousins, on Fox at 1:00 p.m. ET. The only Fox game at 4:25 p.m. ET will be 49ers at Cowboys.

With the Fox pregame show starting at 9:00 a.m. ET, it gives Fox more than 10 hours of continuous NFL broadcasting on Sunday. And with five of the six teams having winning records (and the sixth being the Cowboys), the numbers should start large and keep growing — culminating in a very large audience for the late-afternoon window, which has become the biggest of the NFL week.

item.title: With trade offers rejected, Titans' plans for Tony Pollard come into question
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: All the factors had lined up for a Tony Pollard trade.
item.content:encoded:
All the factors had lined up for a Tony Pollard trade. With a trade not happening, the Titans' future plans for Pollard come into question.

At 1-7, the Titans aren't contenders. Pollard is in the final year of his contract. While a compensatory draft pick becomes possible in 2028 (depending on Tennessee's 2027 free-agent acquisitions and losses), the Titans could have gotten a draft pick in 2027 if they'd traded him.

What could they have gotten? As we hear it, they turned down a fourth-round pick and a player. (The Packers and the Broncos were the two teams linked to Pollard.)

So what's the plan for Pollard? Maybe they want to keep Pollard beyond 2026. He's in the last season of a three-year, $21.75 million deal. He's making $7.25 million this year.

And Pollard is on track for his fifth straight 1,000-yard season. He's not even in the top 20 highest-paid running backs by annual average. The franchise tag at the position for 2027 is expected to be in the range of $15 million.

Pollard will be 30 in April. That makes it harder to put a proper number on his next contract. But if the Titans weren't willing to take the best offer they could get for him, it suggests that they have a plan premised on potentially signing him to a new contract.

The decision to keep Pollard could be as simple as the Titans not being confident in their alternatives. Pollard has 147 touches in eight games. His backup, Tajae Spears, has 33 in six games. Rookie Nick Singleton has seven in four games. Julius Chestnut has no touches in eight games.

The answer could be that simple. The Titans had insufficient confidence in their other options if Pollard was traded. Which would have complicated the ongoing effort to develop quarterback Cam Ward.

Regardless, the Titans had a chance to get something now (we don't know the name of the player that was offered; it could have been a running back) and a 2027 draft pick by trading Pollard. They decided not to.

Pollard will now keep going, and quite possibly finish with more than 1,000 yards again. Which could result in Pollard leaving in 2027 — possibly with the Titans not getting a compensatory draft pick in 2028.

item.title: 49ers will fly to Colorado tonight to begin acclimating to altitude for Mexico City game
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The 49ers won't fly home after today's game in Dallas.
item.content:encoded:
The 49ers won't fly home after today's game in Dallas. Instead, they'll immediately begin preparation for next Sunday night's game in Mexico City.

The team plane will fly to Colorado Springs tonight, as coach Kyle Shanahan believes spending a week at altitude will help the 49ers' chances against the Vikings next week at Estadio Azteca, the highest stadium the NFL ever plays in.

"I think it helps," Shanahan said. "I grew up mainly in Denver, and I know how bad it would be for me. No matter how good of shape you're in, you come home from college and you run up the stairs and you're out of breath. It takes some time to get used to altitude. I know when you go to play in Denver it's always a challenge, and Mexico City is higher than Denver. It's not make or break, but I do think it makes you a couple percent better."

Shanahan thanked Air Force head coach Troy Calhoun for allowing the 49ers to use his team's practice facility in Colorado Springs, as he did before the 49ers' Mexico City game in 2022. Air Force's Falcon Stadium is at 6,621 feet. Estadio Azteca has an altitude of 7,280 feet — exactly 2,000 feet higher than Denver's Mile High elevation.

Next Sunday night will be the 49ers' second international game of the season. They opened the season in Australia, where their decision to arrive a week early to get used to the time difference was credited as one of the reasons for their impressive performance against the Rams. Now they hope another weeklong preparation will yield similar results.

item.title: Arch Manning shakes off 3 interceptions, throws game-winning TD pass as Texas beats LSU
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: As he has been throughout his college football career, Texas quarterback Arch Manning was a mixed bag on Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
As he has been throughout his college football career, Texas quarterback Arch Manning was a mixed bag on Saturday. But Manning and Texas came out on top.

After throwing three interceptions and seeing his team fall behind LSU 21-10, Manning turned it on late, culminating in a 12-play, 58-yard drive that saw Manning throw the game-winning touchdown pass with three seconds remaining as Texas won 22-21.

"That's what college football is all about," Manning said after the game.

Manning's numbers were not impressive: 19-of-35 for 174 yards and one touchdown with three interceptions and four sacks, plus 35 yards and a touchdown running. But when Texas needed him to march the offense down the field at the end of the game, he did it. His touchdown pass to Raleek Brown was a perfectly placed ball, and he also ran for two first downs on the game-winning drive.

For No. 6 Texas, the win means they'll almost certainly be in the College Football Playoff, as they'll be heavy favorites the next two weeks against Arkansas and Texas A&M. For LSU, the loss knocks first-year coach Lane Kiffin out of playoff contention.

Manning, the scion of the first family of quarterbacks, will have an opportunity do what neither his grandfather Archie nor his uncles Peyton and Eli ever did: Win a national championship.

item.title: Lions, Jets renegotiated Andre Cisco trade after concerns arose about his physical
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Broncos-Chargers Daiyan Henley trade wasn't the only one affected by the player's physical.
item.content:encoded:
A controversy arose after the NFL trade deadline when the Broncos demanded to change the terms of their trade with the Chargers after linebacker Daiyan Henley's physical. But Henley wasn't the only traded player whose physical raised concerns.

The Lions also told the Jets they wanted to change the terms of their trade for safety Andre Cisco after concerns about his physical. But unlike the Chargers, the Jets agreed to it, and the Lions ultimately sent the Jets a 2029 sixth-round pick for Cisco after initially agreeing to give up a 2028 sixth-round pick.

Tom Pelissero reports that the modified terms were based on medical concerns. There's no word on what those concerns were, but Lions coach Dan Campbell said the plan is for Cisco to play on Sunday against the Patriots.

The Jets went along with the Lions' request, and in the scheme of things the difference between a 2028 sixth-round pick and a 2029 sixth-round pick is minor. Still, it points to an inherent flaw in the NFL's trade rules: The team acquiring a player has the ability to go back on the trade, or negotiate better terms, after the trade deadline. That puts the team trading the player in a difficult position: After you've already told a player you're trading him, and told another player you're signing him or bringing him up from the practice squad to take his place, you don't want to go back on that. So if the team you're trading with tells you, "We didn't like his physical, so we'll back out of the trade unless you take less compensation," you may feel you have no choice but to accept.

The NFL could resolve that by not allowing trades to be renegotiated after the deadline: Either the player passes the physical and the trade goes through, or the player fails the physical and the trade does not go through. No more half measures like, "We failed him on his physical, but we'll pass the physical if you agree to take a lesser draft pick for him."

Another solution could be that physicals for traded players are conducted by an independent, league-appointed doctor, rather than the team's medical staff. If that doctor says the player passes the physical, the team trading for the player can't back out.

The Jets and Chargers had different reactions to their trade partners asking to renegotiate the trades, but the situation both teams were faced with highlights potential problems that can arise with the NFL allowing teams to change the terms of trades after the trade deadline.

item.title: Three referees will be working in other roles on Sunday, due to the ground stop
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The full scope of the adjustments to the usual officiating crews isn't officially known.
item.content:encoded:
The full scope of the adjustments to the usual officiating crews isn't officially known. It's clear, however, that Friday's nationwide ground stop will result in significant changes to the usual groupings of officiating crews.

On Saturday morning, the NFL announced that three non-referees will serve as referees for four Week 10 games, with one of them — Don Willard — working as the referee for the 1:00 p.m. ET game between the Dolphins and Colts before traveling to Cincinnati for Sunday night's Steelers-Bengals game.

Via Ben Austro of FootballZebras.com, three referees will be working in other roles on Sunday.

Referee Carl Cheffers and referee Alex Kemp will work as umpires. Referee Shawn Hochuli (pictured) will work as a back judge.

The reconfiguration resulted from the NFL's decision to assign officials to games within driving distance of their homes.

Austro also notes that the replay officials for all Sunday games will work out of NFL headquarters. They were in Detroit on Friday for an all-day, in-person training session. Instead of fanning out to the various game locations, they all went to New York.

It sets the stage for a potentially strange day, with any mistakes inevitably being blamed on the inability of the NFL to get the officials where they needed to be. If it works, however, it could prompt the NFL to reconsider the overall staffing plan, if there's a way to do it that reduces expenses.

I think that's a tongue-in-cheek remark. I hope it's a tongue-in-cheek remark.

Either way, Sunday could get interesting. The players and coaches have gotten to where they're supposed to be. The officials haven't, and the deck has been dramatically reshuffled in order to ensure that each game will be properly staffed.

item.title: Game between Bill Belichick's UNC and Louisville ends in a brawl
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Saturday's not alright for fighting.
item.content:encoded:
Saturday's not alright for fighting.

But a fight nevertheless happened at the end of the game between Louisville and Bill Belichick's North Carolina Tar Hells.

The Cardinals led, 16-14, with time ticking away. (UNC had a timeout remaining but hadn't used it on the final Louisville drive, after a game-sealing interception.) Louisville received the snap and took a knee as the clock hit 15 seconds.

North Carolina, despite not using its final timeout, deployed the Schiano-style effort to blow up victory formation. Which sparked a shoving match match between opposing lineman. Which eventually became a full-blown brawl.

Through it all, time expired and the game ended. It will be interesting to see whether the ACC or the individual schools hand out suspensions as a result of the fracas.

The loss dropped North Carolina to 5-5. The Tar Heels need one win in remaining games against Virginia and NC State to become bowl-eligible in Belichick's second season on the job.

And that could be harder to do against Virginia next week, if one or more UNC players end up being required to sit out.

item.title: Chris Jones rejoins Chiefs after traveling on his own to Atlanta
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On Saturday afternoon, the Chiefs announced that defensive tackle Chris Jones would travel on his own to Atlanta for Sunday's game against the Falcons.
item.content:encoded:
On Saturday afternoon, the Chiefs announced that defensive tackle Chris Jones would travel on his own to Atlanta for Sunday's game against the Falcons. On Saturday night, the Chiefs announced that Jones had arrived.

"Chris Jones has rejoined the team in Atlanta," the team said. "He will play tomorrow."

The situation was not injury related; the team attributed it to a personal matter.

It's generally unusual for players to travel on their own to road games. This weekend particularly, individual travel became even more complicated, given the aftermath of Friday's nationwide ground stop.

Regardless, Jones got to where he needed to be, and he'll be playing for the 6-2 Chiefs as they try to match the Broncos, who are on a bye, at 7-2 atop the AFC West.

Harmon had 12 tackles, 1.5 sacks, and a forced fumble in the first four games of the season. The 2025 first-round pick had 27 tackles, three sacks and a fumble recovery during his rookie season.

item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: ESPN hasn't said much about analyst Rex Ryan following his recent arrest in Nashville for running over the feet of two pedestrians with his truck.
item.content:encoded:
ESPN hasn't said much about analyst Rex Ryan following his recent arrest in Nashville for running over the feet of two pedestrians with his truck. It has sparked a question as to whether Ryan will appear on ESPN's Sunday morning pregame show.

“As of now, Rex will appear as scheduled, including on Sunday NFL Countdown,” ESPN said on Saturday night.

It's not believed that Ryan will be addressing the matter on the air.

He faces six misdemeanors as a result of the November 4 incident. He's due in court next month.

Video of the incident reportedly exists. It has yet to be released. It probably will emerge at some point.

Of course, Ryan's presence (or not) may not have even been noticed; with the Patriots and Lions playing at 9:30 a.m. ET, who'll be watching the ESPN pregame show?

item.title: Panthers-Saints game won't have a replay assistant, due to ground stop
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Travel issues will leave at least one game short-staffed.
item.content:encoded:
The nationwide ground stop that shut down the aviation system has impacted the NFL's officiating assignments for Sunday games. And while the league has announced the specific changes that will result in non-referees serving as referees for four games on Sunday (with side judge Don Willard working two games in the same day), other adjustments have not been officially announced.

There surely will be others. For now, one game will be shorthanded.

Via Tom Pelissero of Netflix, the Panthers-Saints game won’t have a replay assistant.

Those duties will be handled by the league office. Which will put a strain on the usual resources there, especially in the cluster of 1:00 p.m. ET games. (Panthers-Saints is one of the seven games to be played in that window.)

Given that the league has otherwise adjusted the Week 10 assignments to keep the officials within driving distance of their hometowns, it's likely that the existing crews will be altered significantly. Which will introduce unfamiliarity and otherwise complicate the effort to get calls right on a consistent basis.

Absent an advance announcement from the league as to the full extent of the changes, they won't be known until the NFL posts the official Game Books for the Sunday contests.

item.title: For Week 9, Jalen Pitre was fined twice for illegal use of helmet
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Every Saturday, plenty of players get fined for illegal use of helmet fouls from the prior weekend's game.
item.content:encoded:
Every Saturday, plenty of players get fined for illegal use of helmet fouls from the prior weekend's game. For Week 9, Texans safety Jalen Pitre got fined twice.

Both instances occurred in the second quarter of the victory over the Chargers. Pitre was penalized for neither infraction.

Each fine will cost $15,400, subject to appeal. They were Pitre's first fines of the season.

For the season (including the preseason), 53 fines have been imposed for illegal use of the helmet.

The NFL will impose larger fines on Pitre for future violations. Eventually, he'll be at risk for a suspension.

Use of the helmet isn't one of the five safety rules that trigger a one-game suspension in the event of three violations.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: It appears quarterback Jacoby Brissett earned a good grade in his crash course on the Ravens offense.
item.content:encoded:
It appears quarterback Jacoby Brissett earned a good grade in his crash course on the Ravens offense.

Brissett joined the team a little over a week ago in a trade with the Cardinals and is on track to start against the Chargers on Monday night. In comments to reporters on Saturday, head coach Jesse Minter didn't make it sound like Brissett will be limited to a small portion of the team's playbook when he takes the field.

"The stuff you heard about was just like, 'Hey, he's a veteran presence and a real pro,'" Minter said, via the team's website. "Obviously, he's been around different systems and things like that. I would just say, I'm very, very impressed with how fast he's learned what we’re doing."

The Ravens head into Monday's game in last place in the AFC North, so they'll need Brissett to operate at a high level right out of the gate to stay in the thick of the playoff race heading into the back half of the season.

item.title: Jakobe Thomas gave Kirk Cousins No. 8 for nothing (other than wins)
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Raiders arguably could have driven a harder bargain over the trade that sent quarterback Kirk Cousins back to the Vikings.
item.content:encoded:
The Raiders arguably could have driven a harder bargain over the trade that sent quarterback Kirk Cousins back to the Vikings. Vikings safety Jakobe Thomas could have driven a harder bargain over the return of Cousins's preferred number.

Thomas told reporters that he gave Cousins No. 8 without payment.

“No money needed,” Thomas said, via Ben Goessling of the Minneapolis Star Tribune. “I just need him to come here and win games. A lot of fans have his jersey anyway, so they could pull him out of the closet and put him back on. So that's all it is. Kirko's got a lot more memories and history in that number than I do, and it's rightfully his. So I just gave it back to his rightful owner.”

Thomas moved to No. 6, the jersey number he wore at Middle Tennessee State.

It makes sense. Thomas, a third-round pick out of Miami in April, has yet to be active for a regular-season game. Cousins is returning with the goal of winning a lot of games.

Starting with Sunday at Lambeau Field, the site of the final game of his first stint with the Vikings.

item.title: Jared Goff takes 1-3 career record vs. Patriots into Germany game
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: For his career, Lions quarterback Jared Goff has a record of 101-67-1 as a starter.
item.content:encoded:
For his career, Lions quarterback Jared Goff has a record of 101-67-1 as a starter. That's a 59.7-percent win rate.

Against the Patriots, Goff is 1-3. That's a 25-percent win rate.

In those four games, Goff has two touchdown passes and five interceptions.

Sunday's game in Germany will be the first one against the Patriots with a coach other than Bill Belichick. Goff has never faced current Patriots coach Mike Vrabel; during Goff's time as a starter with the Rams and Lions and Vrabel's tenure with the Titans, their two teams never crossed paths.

Goff's first loss to New England came in 2016, in his third career start. The Patriots won, 26-10. Two years later, New England beat Goff and the Rams in the Super Bowl, 13-3.

In 2020, Goff and the Rams beat the Patriots, 24-3. In 2022, the Patriots beat Goff and the Lions, 29-0.

Sunday's game is consequential for both teams. The 6-2 Lions are caught in a cluster of four NFC North teams that all have six or more wins. The Patriots, at 5-4, are fading in the AFC East race and could be scrambling to secure a wild-card spot.

item.content:encoded:
Wide receiver Ladd McConkey is among the Chargers players listed as questionable for Monday night's game against the Ravens.

McConkey is dealing with a back injury that kept him off of the practice field this week. McConkey has dealt with a number of injuries this season and has 17 catches for 286 yards and a touchdown on the season.

The Chargers also listed guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), defensive lineman Justin Eboigbe (ankle), tight end David Njoku (fibula), linebacker Denzel Perryman (pectoral), and offensive lineman Trey Pipkins (personal, knee) as questionable. Njoku, Perryman, and Pipkins will need to be activated from injured reserve in order to play against Baltimore.

Wide receiver Brenen Thompson (hamstring) is considered doubtful while guard Branson Taylor (ankle), cornerback Isas Waxter (ankle), and safety Kendall Williamson (calf) have been ruled out.
